category_title: First-grade students who struggle with independent literacy tasks and prefer social or auditory reading
minimal_context: The student is at the workstation during independent work time to self-select a book for reading.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for independent reading. Please go to the workstation and select a book to read.

STUDENT: (Walks to the workstation and immediately grabs a handful of books off the shelf without looking at them.) I got my books.

TUTOR: How did you choose those?

STUDENT: I don't know. Do you have the book you were reading to us earlier? I want that one.

TUTOR: That one is not at the workstation right now. Please pick one from the shelf.

STUDENT: (Drops the first books and grabs another random book off the shelf without looking at the cover or opening the pages.) Okay, I'll just take this one.

options.A: Ignore all undesirable book-grabbing behaviors exhibited by the student while they are at the workstation.
options.B: Break the independent book selection task down into small chunks so that it can be completed.
options.C: Mention a specific book you have been reading or enjoying to help guide the student's selection.
options.D: Implement a DRO plan, providing behavior-specific praise whenever the student engages in alternative behaviors that do not involve grabbing books.
